proposal.policy_prompt_for_action:
Mixed-color goals exposed a SUFFICIENCY failure in the single-color quota rule: a correct aggregate count still led to collecting green after the green quota was complete or abandoning an aligned blue cube. Parse a separate quota for every requested color. Compute each current completed count from its incoming memory plus only that color's release visibly completed in the current motion, exactly once. Only select colors with outstanding quotas; press the button only when every quota is satisfied and the final retreat is complete. For the demonstrated blue-and-green task, collect green while its quota remains outstanding, then blue. Preserve the existing rule to descend onto the already aligned eligible cube instead of changing targets when other cubes appear. Do not treat three aggregate deposits as completion of a three-blue quota.

The generic accessible-cube preference also failed to settle which of several eligible cubes to approach. This is an action-selection SUFFICIENCY problem, not evidence that another historical memory field is needed. Retain clear-grasp feasibility and persistence of an already aligned selection. Do not replace the unspecified tie-breaker with a universal nearest-robot or uppermost-image rule: those rules contradict other recorded selections. A deterministic tie-breaker reproducing all supplied selections remains unresolved by this minibatch; it should not be presented as established by these reports.

Several transfer, release, retreat, and button approaches selected the correct operation but missed its world position. Strengthen calibrated localization rather than adding position memory. Back-project cube top-face centers at approximately z=0.04 and use their world xy for the z=0.02 grasp. Recover the bin opening's geometric center using its elevated rim and visible opposing edges, checking front and wrist views together; do not intersect the dark opening center with the tabletop or substitute the centroid of its unoccluded fragment. Under partial occlusion, fit the opening geometry from visible rim segments and the other current view. The opening reference height must be established from that geometry rather than an invented numerical height. Back-project the gray button-top center at approximately z=0.02, not z=0, and use that xy for approach and press.

Make the distinction between target geometry and measured TCP explicit. After a closed-hand transfer reaches approximately z=0.20, re-localize the opening and command open at [bin_x, bin_y, 0.20], correcting residual lateral error in that waypoint. Add a 3 mm vertical displacement only when the centered target would otherwise produce no motion. After release, retreat open to [bin_x-0.10, bin_y, 0.20], using the visually localized bin center, never current TCP xy minus 0.10. Retain the mandatory retreat after the final deposit, and retain the existing grasp, lift, separate closed transfer/opening, button-close, press, and contact-retraction rules.

Remove the requirement to normalize cube-edge yaw into approximately [-0.7854,0.7854]. Valid recorded edge-aligned grasps exceed that interval. Choose a downward, edge-aligned feasible grasp orientation for the selected cube, preserve it through descent and lift, and preserve the measured grasp orientation during transport. Re-estimate edge alignment for a newly selected cube rather than retaining the previous cube's yaw.
proposal.refused: The initial mixed-color report described the selected cube as blue and proposed starting with blue. The wrist view at approach and the subsequent grasp, transport, and release show green; the first two deposits were green and the next three blue. The blue-first interpretation is therefore rejected. Reports proposing nearest-robot or uppermost-image selection are not promoted to a universal rule: an initial green selection chose a different cube from the robot-nearest one, and a later red selection did not choose the uppermost visible red cube. Exact per-scene target coordinates cannot supply a general visible tie-breaker, so those coordinate-specific prescriptions are not passed on as policy rules. Claims that centered release and bin-relative retreat were wholly absent are also overstated: both existed in the previous instruction. Their demonstrated confusion warrants the explicit target-versus-measured-TCP clarification, not an additional phase field or stored bin position. No numeric bin-rim height is supplied because the reports do not establish one.

policy_prompt_for_action.modify_from: Read the requested color and quantity N from the goal each cycle. Use deposited_count plus any release visibly completed in the current incoming motion to determine how many deposits are now complete; do not count a release twice. Start with an open hand and zero deposits.
policy_prompt_for_action.modify_to: Read a separate quota for each requested color from the goal each cycle. For each color, compute its completed count from its incoming deposited_<color> memory plus only that color's release visibly completed in the current incoming motion, exactly once, as in the memory update. Do not add the release again to an already updated count. A color is eligible only while its own quota remains outstanding. Completion requires every requested color's quota to be satisfied. Start with an open hand and zero deposits for each requested color.

policy_prompt_for_action.modify_from: Infer object positions from calibrated front and wrist views, using the tabletop plane and cube geometry rather than treating image coordinates as world coordinates. Cubes are approximately 4 cm wide. Locate the bin by its opening and the stop button by its gray circular top on a light square base. Re-estimate positions from current views; scene objects can appear during execution. Robot right is negative world y.
policy_prompt_for_action.modify_to: Infer object positions from calibrated front and wrist views rather than treating image coordinates as world coordinates. Cubes are approximately 4 cm wide: back-project their top-face centers at approximately z=0.04 and use the resulting world xy for the z=0.02 grasp. Locate the bin opening's geometric center from its elevated rim and opposing edges, checking both current views. Under partial occlusion, fit the opening geometry from visible rim segments and the other view; do not use the centroid of the visible dark fragment or intersect the opening center with the tabletop. Establish the opening reference height from observed geometry, not an assumed numeric rim height. Locate the button by its gray circular top on a light square base; back-project the top center at approximately z=0.02 and use that xy for approach and press. texts.action:
Read a separate quota for each requested color from the goal each cycle. For each color, compute its completed count from its incoming deposited_<color> memory plus only that color's release visibly completed in the current incoming motion, exactly once, as in the memory update. Do not add the release again to an already updated count. A color is eligible only while its own quota remains outstanding. Completion requires every requested color's quota to be satisfied. Start with an open hand and zero deposits for each requested color. Infer object positions from calibrated front and wrist views rather than treating image coordinates as world coordinates. Cubes are approximately 4 cm wide: back-project their top-face centers at approximately z=0.04 and use the resulting world xy for the z=0.02 grasp. Locate the bin opening's geometric center from its elevated rim and opposing edges, checking both current views. Under partial occlusion, fit the opening geometry from visible rim segments and the other view; do not use the centroid of the visible dark fragment or intersect the opening center with the tabletop. Establish the opening reference height from observed geometry, not an assumed numeric rim height. Locate the button by its gray circular top on a light square base; back-project the top center at approximately z=0.02 and use that xy for approach and press. Re-estimate positions from current views; scene objects can appear during execution. Robot right is negative world y.

When any color quota remains outstanding and the hand is empty away from the bin's release position, select a visible, accessible tabletop cube of an eligible color. Prefer a clear grasp and maintain the selection when the hand is already aligned above an eligible cube; do not switch cubes or colors simply because new cubes appear. Never select another cube of a color whose quota is already satisfied. Approach its center at z=0.15 with the gripper open, roll=-3.1416, pitch=0, and a feasible yaw aligned with a cube edge. Do not constrain yaw to [-0.7854,0.7854]. Re-estimate edge alignment for each newly selected cube rather than carrying over the previous cube's yaw, and preserve the selected orientation through descent and lift. When already above that cube near z=0.15, descend to its center at z=0.02 and close. Use the wrist view to refine the same cube's center rather than descending at an inaccurate reported approach position.

When a cube is grasped at table height, lift vertically to z=0.15, retaining its grasp orientation and keeping the gripper closed. A cube between the fingers and finger positions around 0.018 m support a successful grasp. Once lifted, move to the visually localized world xy center of the bin opening at z=0.20, keeping the cube closed in the gripper and preserving the measured grasp orientation. After the closed-hand transfer reaches approximately z=0.20 above the bin, re-localize the opening and command open at [bin_x, bin_y, 0.20], correcting any residual lateral error in that waypoint. The target is the opening center, not the measured TCP xy. Opening remains a separate operation from the closed-hand transfer. Add a 0.003 m vertical displacement only if the centered target would otherwise produce no motion.

When the hand is empty and open at the bin after a release, retreat toward the robot: target [bin_x-0.10, bin_y, 0.20], preserving orientation and keeping open. Compute this offset from the visually localized bin center, never from measured TCP xy. Perform this retreat even after the final requested cube. If the incoming motion already included this retreat and the hand is at that offset, do not repeat it. Retreat clears the opening and gives the dropped cube time to fall; no separate arbitrary wait is needed.

When every requested color's quota is satisfied and the final release retreat is finished, ignore all remaining cubes. Approach the button center at z=0.15, roll=-3.1416, pitch=0, yaw=0, with the gripper open. When already aligned above the button with open fingers, close the empty gripper at that approach position, adding a 0.003 m vertical displacement if needed to ensure a nonzero motion. When aligned above the button with closed fingers, descend to [button_x, button_y, 0.0075] with the gripper closed. If the current motion shows this descent reaching button contact, retract to [button_x, button_y, 0.15] with the gripper still closed. Contact can leave the measured TCP near z=0.0245 rather than the commanded depth; recognize the visible contact and retract instead of repeatedly demanding a deeper press.

For an unanticipated or ambiguous situation, use the visible hand contents, finger opening, height, and object alignment to recover the applicable rule. Never increase the deposit count without an observed release. If a grasp fails, reopen with a small nonzero upward motion and re-approach a visible requested-color cube. If any color quota remains outstanding but no suitable cube of an eligible color is currently available, wait 16 control steps specifically to observe newly arriving cubes, then reassess. If an object needed for localization is occluded, move upward to a clear viewing height while retaining any held cube, then re-localize. Never press the stop button before every requested color's quota is satisfied and the final release retreat is complete.
